Alan Turing was an English mathematician and logician, widely regarded as the father of theoretical computer science. He was born in 1912 and passed away in 1954. Turing formalized the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine, which is a model of a general-purpose computer. 

His contributions to cryptanalysis were significant during World War II, as he helped the Allies decipher messages encrypted by the German Enigma machine. Additionally, Turing introduced the Turing test, which is a concept in the philosophy of artificial intelligence, and he also contributed to the Turing pattern concept in mathematical and theoretical biology.

For more detailed information, you can visit his [Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Turing).
